perturbation.perturbation_definition: remove an order that is INVISIBLE at the decision clock while the revealed prefix is bit-identical

r1_event_identity.conclusion: R1 must select on reveal_idx (order-reveal events), NEVER on event_id (which also counts service completions, returns and the booking end)

verdict.mandatory_condition: the L1 collector MUST construct StrictOnlineEnv with an explicit, pre-specified public booking_horizon = 24.0 (the data generator declaration at generate_coldchain_data.py:119, which covers every reveal; the pilot constant 16.0 would truncate this data and is rejected); with the None default the baseline WAIT/CLOSE decision reads real future reveal data and the state may NOT be labelled STRICT_ONLINE_QUALIFIED

rows.name: G1 JF1-H-F consumes has_future_reveal and the constructor default is booking_horizon=None
G2 with booking_horizon=None the WAIT/CLOSE answer FLIPS when the unrevealed future is perturbed while the revealed prefix is fixed (the leak the user identified)
G3 with booking_horizon=16.0 the answer is INVARIANT under the same perturbation (decision-visible future information eliminated by construction)
G3b timing-only perturbations do NOT expose the leak at horizon=None (it is sensitivity to the EXISTENCE of a future reveal, not to its timing), so the horizon is what removes it
G4 the horizon branch is a clean public predicate: True before the booking deadline and False at/after it
G5 R1 slots must be keyed on reveal_idx, not event_id: event_id counts physical events (service completion / return / booking end) and reveal_events is a de-duplicated set
G6 R1 x K=4 slots enumerated on dev_check (slot count is a pre-registered slot budget, not a promise of K qualified snapshots per instance)
